profile.headline: SWE @ Apple | UBC CS 2023
profile.summary:
I love to learn and explore new topics in computer science and I especially enjoy systems and other low-level programming. I am most experienced in C, C++, and x86_64 Assembly. I've used many other languages for specific projects; I don't limit myself to just my favourites.

I’m starting a new adventure in a new state in January. I’m really excited to work on a team that aligns so closely with my skills and interests. In addition to work, I enjoy a lot of self-directed learning, tinkering, and experimenting on my own time. For example, I:

- Stay current reading blogs and manuals on low-level details of processors (such as LLVM Weekly, the Intel Architecture Manual, Maynard Handley's M1 Exploration, and Travis Downs' blog Performance Matters)
- Keep a few servers and other equipment co-located in Hurricane Electric's Fremont 2 datacentre in Fremont California
- Maintain Virtual Machines in various locations hosted by people I have met online 
- Have my own ASN which I use for experimenting with networking

Outside of technical interests, I also enjoy playing the flute, artistic swimming, skiing, and photography.

positions.title: Junior Software Engineer
positions.description:
At Old Mission, I specialized in networking and performance optimization, focusing on enhancing their systems at a low level. I expanded their code generation system for network protocols, enabling support for complex, non-static message layouts. This improved the flexibility of their networking stack.

In addition, I undertook several projects aimed at optimizing packet processing applications. By analyzing caching behavior and minimizing branch prediction penalties, I successfully improved their performance and efficiency.

My primary project involved integrating a sophisticated kernel bypass library into our codebase, which greatly enhanced network performance compared to the standard vendor-provided POSIX socket interception. This integration was deployed across all networking applications developed by the team I was on. Beyond the basic implementation, I utilized Linux’s ethtool ioctl and sysfs interfaces to ensure proper network card configuration, set CPU affinities for interrupts, and access detailed status and statistics for debugging—capabilities beyond the reach of standard Linux tools.

positions.title: Software Development Intern
positions.description:
At Thekla Inc., I contributed to the development of the Jai programming language, focusing on its compiler and built-in libraries. Collaborating closely with Jonathan Blow, I played a key role in writing a library for asynchronous file I/O and improving the Unicode library's compliance, ensuring accurate conversions between UTF-8, UTF-16, and UTF-32.

I also contributed to various other libraries, including those for atomics and synchronization. Although my primary focus was not on adding new features to the compiler, I frequently fixed bugs and made enhancements, particularly in the areas of C and Objective-C interoperability. The Jai compiler features an LLVM backend, a native x64 backend, and an integrated assembler, which I leveraged to optimize performance and functionality.

The company is using Jai to develop an upcoming video game called Sokoban. While I was not deeply involved in the game's development, I occasionally implemented features in the libraries I developed or improved, and participated in play-testing and code reviews to identify potential enhancements for the language and its libraries.

positions.title: Teaching Assistant
positions.description:
As a Teaching Assistant for CPSC 203 and CPSC 259, I facilitated courses designed for students outside the computer science discipline. In CPSC 203, I collaborated directly with Dr. Cinda Heeren to create course materials, introducing programming in Python and foundational concepts in data structures and algorithms to a diverse student body from across the university.

In CPSC 259, I focused on teaching data structures and algorithms to electrical engineering students. My instruction emphasized the use of pointers and the differences between the stack, heap, and static data, providing these students with a solid understanding of crucial programming concepts.

positions.title: Head of Facilities and Pool Maintenance
positions.description:
As a Certified Pool Operator, I collaborated with my team to maintain pool chemical balance and cleanliness in compliance with Public Health Standards. My responsibilities included building, repairing, and maintaining equipment, facilities, and grounds as needed, ensuring the entire facility remained safe for public use.

I interacted with members to ensure their safety and well-being, and trained new employees, teaching a leadership course for future staff members. I was also entrusted with the master keys to the building and staff lockers, reflecting the high level of trust and responsibility placed in me.

positions.title: Research Assistant
positions.description: Under the direction of Dr. Denise Daley and her research team, I developed data processing systems for ongoing genetic research projects. My primary responsibilities included updating a large Java project to accommodate new research data and creating data processing shell scripts to be executed on a computing cluster.

honors.title: Dean’s Honour List
honors.description:
I was privileged to be included on the Dean’s Honour List for my first three years at The University of British Columbia. This accolade is awarded to students who maintain an outstanding academic record, specifically achieving a standing of 80% or better in the previous Winter Session while carrying a course load of at least 27 percentage-graded credits. My consistent performance in my courses reflected my dedication and hard work, culminating in this prestigious recognition.

Although I did not meet the course load requirement in my fourth year due to my engagement in advanced projects and research, I graduated with distinction. This indicates that I maintained an average of at least 80% over my upper-level core classes. The Dean’s Honour List recognition underscored my academic excellence and dedication to my studies, and it remains a testament to my commitment to academic rigour and achievement.
honors.issuer: Issued by University of British Columbia · Apr 2022

honors.title: 2021 Technology Impact Awards Scholarship
honors.description: In July 2021, I was honoured to receive the prestigious Technology Impact Awards Scholarship from the BC Tech Association. This recognition came with a generous $3,500 scholarship, underscoring my commitment to technological innovation and excellence in my academic pursuits at The University of British Columbia. The BC Tech Association's acknowledgement of my work serves as a significant milestone in my educational journey, reflecting the potential and promise seen in my contributions to the tech community. For more details on this award and its recipients, you can visit the BC Tech Association's website: https://wearebctech.com/bc-tech-reveals-the-2021-technology-impact-awards-scholarship-recipients/
honors.issuer: Issued by BC Tech Association · Jul 2021

volunteerExperiences.role: Computer Science Department Student Development Committee Member
volunteerExperiences.description:
As a member of the Student Development Committee, I collaborated with professors, staff, and fellow students to plan events for the entire computer science department. I played a key role in transitioning events to an online format by researching alternatives to Zoom and ultimately selecting Gather.Town for its interactive capabilities. I created virtual worlds that were used for events throughout the year.

In my final year in this role, I liaised with student-run clubs to determine how the department could best support them, particularly in the areas of funding and sponsorship.

As a Workshop Leader at the Ocean Park Community Orchard, I was involved in the initial proposal to the City of Surrey to create the orchard, aiming to promote community cohesiveness and provide food to the local Surrey Food Bank. Following the approval, I actively participated in planting, weeding, watering, beekeeping, special events, and art installations.

In 2018, I began conducting workshops on garden photography for seniors' groups, sharing my knowledge and fostering a sense of community engagement.

testScores.name: AP Computer Science
testScores.description: I took the AP Computer Science Class through BC Online School during the 2018-2019 school year. In May, I took the AP exam and achieved a score of 5/5, the highest score possible. My teacher described me as "one of the strongest and most creative students that I have had" and gave me the opportunity to review an upcoming course module on Swing.

testScores.name: SAT Subject Test in Mathematics Level 1 & 2
testScores.description: In preparation for applying to universities, I took the SAT subject tests in Math I and Math II. I achieved a score of 760 on Math I and a perfect score of 800 on Math II. I completed both exams with plenty of time to spare.
